description.narrative:
This project is a collaborative initiative between the United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA), the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO), and the Spanish Agency for International Cooperation (AECID). Its main objective is to strengthen the identity and capacities of Afro-Mexican youth in Mexico, particularly adolescents and young women. It will focus on promoting their human rights, including sexual and reproductive rights, gender equality, interculturality, and the fight against racism and discrimination.
The project will be implemented primarily in the states of Guerrero and Oaxaca (Costa Chica region). A platform for intersectoral dialogue will be established to advance the rights of this population. A participatory assessment will be developed based on the methodologies of the Unidas Crecemos and Generación 2030 projects, promoted by UNFPA. Awareness-raising campaigns, training workshops, and community projects will be developed to empower them to access their rights. The project will begin with an initial implementation phase lasting 18 months and is aligned with Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) 3, 4, 5, 10, 11, and 17.
